llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate Positionstack connector skill, but its setup instructions include unsafe remote installer commands that deserve review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The declared tool access is narrow, Bash(oo *), and fits connector use; however, the documented installer commands fall outside that narrow oo-only operational scope.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The first-time setup section tells the agent to install the oo CLI using curl piped to bash and PowerShell irm piped to iex, with no version pinning, checksum, signature verification, or explicit user handoff.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger wording is broad for any Positionstack request, but the runtime instructions constrain use to the positionstack connector actions and require live schema inspection before payload construction.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installing the CLI and running oo auth login can create persistent local tooling or authenticated state. That is purpose-related, but the install/auth setup path is under-scoped for the authority it may grant.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: use the OOMOL oo CLI to call Positionstack forward and reverse geocoding actions through a connected account. The action list is limited to read-style geocoding operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the setup path before installing. Prefer installing the oo CLI from verified official documentation with version or integrity checks, and only connect Positionstack or sign in when you intentionally want this skill to use your OOMOL-connected Positionstack account.
llm.findings:
[SC2] unexpected: The skill needs the oo CLI, but directly executing remote installer scripts is not proportionate to the connector purpose without verification or a clear user-controlled install step.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad activation wording is imprecise, but it is service-specific and the artifact only lists forward_geocode and reverse_geocode actions, so this is a scoping note rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
